sentences.text: Ms. T. H. Udeshi, A.G.P. for Appellant No.1.
Mr. Tariq M. Zahee, Advocate for Appellant No.2.
Ms. Rajkumari Rai, Advocate for Respondents.

CORAM : MRS.VRUSHALI V. JOSHI, J.
RESERVED ON : OCTOBER 30th, 2023 PRONOUNCED ON : DECEMBER 11th, 2023 JUDGMENT 1.

Being aggrieved by the judgment and order passed by the Joint Civil Judge, Senior Division,
Nagpur in Land Acquisition Case No. 65/1998, the appellants have filed the appeal for granting exorbitant compensation to the respondents.
The respondents have also filed the cross-objection being not satisfied with the amount of compensation granted for the land and calculating it covered with the trees.
2. The notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act was published in official gazette on 27.04.1995 for the land admeasuring 6.54 H.R., Orange trees and other trees thereon.

The land was acquired by award dated 30.04.1997 in Land Acquisition Case No.2/A-65/1992-93 of mounza Ridhora in which the land owned by the deceased respondent i.e. claimant admeasuring total 3.54 H.R. and trees 3/7 FA.434.2004-J.odt thereon was acquired.
The respondent was paid compensation to the tune of Rs.16,43,422/- for the said land including cost of land, trees and solatium and interest.
3. The respondents filed reference application for enhancement of compensation before the Collector, Nagpur and claimed additional compensation.

The Joint Civil Judge, Senior Division,
Nagpur partly allowed the reference and determined the value of total 3.54 hectares out of total 6.54 hectares land at the rate of Rs.2,50,000/- per hectare and granted compensation at the rate of Rs.2,500/- per Orange tree for 1150 Orange trees, Rs.4000/- for one Mango tree, Rs. 1000/- per tree for 14 Lemon trees.

4. During the pendency of the appeal, the First Appeal No.699/2015 with Cross Objection No.52/2016 was decided on 14.12.2020 enhancing the compensation for 1150 Orange trees at the rate of Rs.5000/- per tree by this Court.
The First Appeal No.699/2015 with Cross Objection No.52/2016

was ariseing out of the Land Acquisition Case No.133/2008 arising out of same award dated 30.04.1997 of mouza Ridhora in respect of land at Survey No.264 and 305, which were Spl.Land Acq.Officer (Kanholi Naka ... vs Yogesh Waman Satpute And 2 Others on 11 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53045880/
2 acquired for the same project and situated in same village Ridhora and were within the vicinity of each other having same potential.
4/7 FA.434.2004-J.odt 5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard both the learned Counsel and the learned Counsel for the cross objector Ms. Rai.

6. As per judgment of Ambya Kalya Mhatre (dead) through LRs and others Vs. State of Maharashtra, reported in 2012 (1) Mh.L.J. 9, in which the Hon'ble Apex Court has held in that separate compensation for fruit bearing trees and land shall be granted and, therefore, the respondent No.1 is entitled for separate compensation for the acquired land.

entities.text: Ambya Kalya Mhatre (dead) through LRs and others Vs. State of Maharashtra, reported in 2012 (1) Mh.L.J. 9
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. The reference Court ought to have granted compensation at the rate of Rs.5000/- per Orange tree.
7/12 extract indicates presence of 1150 Orange trees along with some other trees.

According to him,
the First Appeal No.699/2015 and Cross Objection No.52/2016 decided on 14.12.2020 by this Court has held the claimants entitled for the compensation of Rs.5000/- per Orange tree on the basis of number of trees recorded in 7/12 extracts.
8. The cross objector has also relied on the judgment of Vidarbha Irrigation Development Corporation, Nagpur Vs. Champatrao s/o.

entities.text: Vidarbha Irrigation Development Corporation, Nagpur Vs. Champatrao
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Amrutrao Bhaswar reported in 2020 (4) Mh.L.J. 297 along with cross objection.
In which the Court has consider the separate compensation for fruit bearing trees and land.
The learned Counsel has submitted that the 5/7 FA.434.2004-J.odt claimants are entitled for similar rate for Orange trees and separate compensation for land as per the said judgment.

9. The following point arises for determination :
"Whether the judgment of the reference Court deserves to be modified ?"
10.
On perusal of the records of the case.
It is seen that the claimants led evidence that there were 1150 Orange trees.

650 Orange trees aged about 8 years and 500 Orange trees about 5 years old at the time of acquisition of the land, at the time of notice under Section 4 of the Act and this fact is not disputed in the cross-examination of the claimant by the defence Counsel.
Moreover, Land Acquisition Officer has admitted in the JMR Exhibit -22 about number of Orange trees which were standing in the land of claimant Survey No.310 at the time of acquisition of the land.

The claimant has proved in his evidence which is supported with the documents, 7/12 extracts and old receipt of payment of water charges for use of water from river and hence the compensation for his perennial irrigated land at the rate of Rs. 2,50,000/- per hectare.
While observing, the reference Court has stated that out of total 6.54 hectare land, the claimant has claimed cost for fruit bearing Orange trees.
There was one farm house/cattle shed.

The reference Court has adopted the value of Orange trees in Land Acquisition Case No.43/1999 and granted Rs.2,500/-
6/7 FA.434.2004-J.odt per tree for 1150 Orange trees, Rs.700/- for one Karwand tree, Rs.4000/-
for per Mango tree, Rs.1000/- per Guava tree and Rs. 1000/- per Lamon tree and Rs. 400/- for per Spl.Land Acq.Officer (Kanholi Naka ... vs Yogesh Waman Satpute And 2 Others on 11 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53045880/
3 Subhabul tree.
11.

entities.text: Kanholi Naka ... vs Yogesh Waman Satpute And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As regards the rate of compensation for Orange trees is concerned, it is seen that the valuer has found an amount of Rs.3,925/- per tree as just compensation in his award.
The reference Court however has granted Rs.2,500/- per tree.
In First Appeal No.699/2015, Rs.5000/- per tree amount of compensation for the Orange trees is reasonable considering the nature of crop in that part of the area.
The cross objector relying on the report of the valuer has conceded for Rs.3,900/- per tree.
To that extent and to the extent that the separate compensation for land covered with the trees is not considered by the reference Court.
Hence, to that extent also, the judgment of the reference Court deserves modification.
The point as framed is answered accordingly.
12. The judgment of reference Court is partly modified.

13. The appellant No.2 is directed to pay compensation at the rate of Rs.2,50,000/- per hectare for remaining three hectares acquired land of the respondents - cross objectors along with all statutory benefits deducting the statutory benefits and interest on the delayed period.
The appellant No.2 is directed to pay compensation at the rate of Rs.3,900/- per tree for Orange tree.
15. All compensation shall be paid along with interest excluding the delayed period.

16. The other part of the judgment in respect of other trees is maintained.
17.
The amount of compensation deposited/paid by the appellants, Nagpur be deducted from the amount payable to the respondent No.1.
18. The respondent No.1 shall submit calculation of amount to the appellants.
After receipt of calculation, the Executive Engineer, Lower Wanna Project, Wardha is directed to deposit the amount of compensation before this Court within a period of six months.
19. The appeal and cross objection stand disposed of.
No costs.
